61.h: 57 - Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb ibn Nufayl ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Riyāḥ al-ʿAdawī * ⟦1:297⟧
61.t:
The master, the martyr, the fighter in the cause of Allah, the God-fearing, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Qurashī al-ʿAdawī, brother of the Commander of the Faithful (أمير المؤمنين) ʿUmar.
He was older than ʿUmar and accepted Islam before him.
He was dark-skinned and very tall. He witnessed Badr and the other campaigns, and the Prophet ﷺ had made a pact of brotherhood between him and Maʿn ibn ʿAdī al-ʿAjlānī.
On the day of Badr ʿUmar said to him: Put on my coat of mail.
He said: I want from martyrdom what you want.
He said: So both of them left it. The banner of the Muslims was with him on the day of al-Yamāmah, and he kept advancing with it into the throat of the enemy, then fought until he was killed. The banner fell, and Sālim, the client (المولى) of Abū Ḥudhayfah, took it.
ʿUmar grieved over him and used to say: He accepted Islam before me, and he was martyred before me.
He used to say: The east wind never blows but I find the scent of Zayd.
Narrating from him: ابن أخيه عبد الله بن عمر, the report on the prohibition of killing the dwellers of the houses (1) .
Narrating from him: ولده عبد الرحمن بن زيد, two hadiths.
He was martyred in Rabīʿ al-Awwal, in the year 12.

62.h: 58 - Asʿad ibn Zurārah ibn ʿUdas ibn ʿUbayd ibn Thaʿlabah al-Anṣārī *
62.t:
Ibn Ghanm ibn Mālik ibn al-Najjār.
The master, the chief of Banū al-Najjār, Abū Umāmah al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī, one of the great Companions (الصحابي). ⟦1:299⟧
He died as a martyr of the throat ailment (1) , and after him the Prophet ﷺ appointed no chief over Banū al-Najjār.
He said: (I am your chief).
So they used to take pride in that (2) .
Ibn Isḥāq said: He died while the Prophet ﷺ was building his mosque, before Badr.
Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Daghūlī said:
It is said that he met the Prophet ﷺ in Mecca a year before the First ʿAqabah, with five men of the Khazraj, and they believed in him.
When they came to Medina, they spoke of Islam among their people. The following year twelve men of them went out, and that was the First ʿAqabah, and they returned with them.
The Prophet ﷺ sent Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr to teach them the recitation and instruct them in religion.
Ibn Isḥāq said: حدثنا محمد بن أبي أمامة بن سهل، عن عبد الرحمن بن كعب بن مالك، قال:
I was the guide of my father when he went blind. When I took him out to the Friday prayer and he heard the call to prayer, he would pray for Abū Umāmah and ask forgiveness for him.
I said: Father! What do you think of your asking forgiveness for Abū Umāmah whenever you hear the call to prayer on Friday, what is it about?
He said: My son! He was the first to lead us in the Friday prayer in Medina, in the lowland of al-Nabīt, in the stony tract of Banū Bayāḍah, at a place called Naqīʿ al-Khaḍamāt (3) .
I said: How many were you that day?
He said: Forty men. Asʿad was the foremost of the twelve chiefs, and he was the chief of Banū al-Najjār, and Usayd ibn al-Ḥuḍayr was chief of Banū ⟦1:300⟧ ʿAbd al-Ashhal, and Abū al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihān al-Balawī, of the allies of Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal, and Saʿd ibn Khaythamah al-Awsī, one of Banū Ghanm ibn Salm, and Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ al-Khazrajī al-Ḥārithī, who was killed on the day of Uḥud, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah ibn Thaʿlabah al-Khazrajī al-Ḥārithī, who was killed on the day (1) of Muʾtah, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥarām Abū Jābir al-Salamī, chief of Banū Salimah, and Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah ibn Dulaym al-Khazrajī al-Sāʿidī, a leader and chief, and al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr al-Sāʿidī the chief, who was killed on the day of Biʾr Maʿūnah, and al-Barāʾ ibn Maʿrūr al-Khazrajī al-Salamī, and ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit al-Khazrajī, of the Qawāqilah (2) , and Rāfiʿ ibn Mālik al-Khazrajī al-Zuraqī (may Allah be pleased with them (3)).
He narrated: شعبة، عن محمد بن عبد الرحمن:
That his grandfather Asʿad ibn Zurārah was struck by the pain of the throat ailment in his throat.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (I will certainly do my utmost, or I will excuse myself regarding Abū Umāmah).
So he cauterised him with his own hand, and he died.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (An evil death for the Jews! They say: Why did he not ward it off from his companion? And I have no power for him, nor for myself, against anything from Allah) (4) . ⟦1:301⟧
It is said that he died in the first year of the Hijrah (may Allah be pleased with him), and in that year three of the great men of the Jāhiliyyah (الجاهلية) and elders of Quraysh died:
al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī, father of ʿAmr, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah al-Makhzūmī, father of Khālid, and Abū Uḥayḥah Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ al-Umawī.
Al-Wāqidī said: Maʿmar narrated to me, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Umāmah ibn Sahl, who said:
They were twelve chiefs, headed by Asʿad ibn Zurārah (1) .
And from ʿUmar, from ʿĀʾishah, who said:
The Prophet ﷺ made Asʿad chief over the chiefs.
And from Khubayb ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said:
Asʿad ibn Zurārah and Dhakwān ibn ʿAbd Qays went out to Mecca, to ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah, and heard of the Messenger of Allah. They came to him, and he presented Islam to them and recited the Qurʾān to them, and they accepted Islam. They were the first to come to Medina with Islam (2) .
And from Umm Khārijah: al-Nawwār, mother of Zayd ibn Thābit, informed me that she saw Asʿad ibn Zurārah, before the arrival of the Prophet ﷺ, leading the people in the five prayers, gathering them in a mosque he had built.
She said: I look at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he arrived: he prayed in that mosque and built it up, and it is his mosque today (3) .
Isrāʾīl narrated from Manṣūr, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: The throat ailment seized Asʿad ibn ⟦1:302⟧ Zurārah, and the Prophet ﷺ came to him and said: (Be cauterised, for I do not blame myself over you) (1) .
زهير بن معاوية: عن أبي الزبير، عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن بعض الصحابة، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cauterised Asʿad twice in his throat for the throat ailment, and said: (I leave no distress in myself over him) (2) .
الثوري: عن أبي الزبير، عن جابر، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cauterised him twice on his main vein.
It is said: He cauterised him and so encircled his throat with it, meaning with the cautery (3) .
It is said: Asʿad entrusted his daughters to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they were three. They were in the care of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and went round with him among the houses of his wives. They are Furayʿah, Kabshah and Ḥabībah. Jewellery containing gold and pearls came to him, and he adorned them with it (4) .
And from Ibn Abī al-Rijāl, who said:
Banū al-Najjār came and said: Our chief Asʿad has died, so appoint a chief over us, O Messenger of Allah.
He said: (I am your chief (5)).
Al-Wāqidī said: The Anṣār say: The first to be buried in al-Baqīʿ was Asʿad.
And the Muhājirūn say: The first to be buried in it was ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn. ⟦1:303⟧
And from Abū Umāmah ibn Sahl:
That the Prophet ﷺ visited Asʿad when the thorn-disease had seized him, and ordered that he be cauterised, so a ring of cautery was made around his neck. He did not last but a short time before he died (may Allah be pleased with him) (1) .

63.h: 59 - ʿUtbah ibn Ghazwān * ibn Jābir ibn Wuhayb Abū Ghazwān al-Māzinī
63.t:
The master, the commander, the fighter in the cause of Allah, Abū Ghazwān al-Māzinī, ally of Banū ʿAbd Shams.
He accepted Islam as the seventh of seven in Islam, and migrated to Abyssinia, then witnessed Badr and the other campaigns. He was one of the celebrated archers and one of the commanders of the raiders, and he is the one who laid out and founded Basra.
Narrating from him: خالد بن عمير العدوي، وقبيصة بن جابر، وهارون بن رئاب، والحسن البصري، ولم يلقاه، وغنيم بن قيس المازني.
It is said that his patronymic (الكنية) was: Abū ʿAbd Allāh. ⟦1:304⟧
ابن سعد: أنبأنا محمد بن عمر، حدثنا جبير بن عبد الله، وإبراهيم بن عبد الله من ولد عتبة بن غزوان، قالا:
ʿUmar appointed ʿUtbah ibn Ghazwān over Basra. He is the one who made Basra a garrison city and laid it out. Before it the place was al-Ubullah. He built the mosque with reeds and built no house in it (1) .
It is said: Basra was formerly called the land of India. The first to settle it was ʿUtbah, with eight hundred men. It was named Basra after black stones that were there. When they became numerous, they built seven mud-brick quarters, two of them in al-Khurayba. Its people used to raid the mountains of Persia.
Ibn Saʿd said: Saʿd used to write to ʿUtbah while he was his governor, and ʿUtbah resented that, and asked ʿUmar for permission to come to him. He granted permission, and ʿUtbah appointed al-Mughīrah as his deputy over Basra. He complained to ʿUmar of Saʿd's domineering over him, but ʿUmar was silent, so ʿUtbah repeated it and said much.
He said: What harm is it to you, ʿUtbah, to submit the matter to a man of Quraysh?
He said: Am I not of Quraysh?
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (The ally of a people is one of them (2)), and I have an old companionship. He said: We do not ⟦1:305⟧ deny that of your merit.
He said: Since the matter has come to this, then by Allah I shall never return to Basra.
ʿUmar refused and sent him back, and he died on the road, struck by a stomach illness.
His servant Suwayd brought his estate to ʿUmar, and that was in the year 17 (may Allah be pleased with him).
He died on the road to Basra, travelling as a delegate to Medina, in the year 17.
It is said: He died in the year 15, and lived fifty-seven years (may Allah be pleased with him).
He has a hadith in the Ṣaḥīḥ of Muslim.
أبو نعامة السعدي: عن خالد بن عمير، وشويس (1) ، قالا:
ʿUtbah ibn Ghazwān addressed us and said:
Indeed, the world has announced its departure, and has turned away swiftly (2) , and nothing of it remains except a dreg like the dreg left in a vessel. You are in a house from which you will be transferred, so move on with the best of what is at hand ... and he mentioned the hadith (3) . ⟦1:306⟧

64.h: 60 - ʿUkkāshah ibn Miḥṣan Abū Miḥṣan al-Asadī *
64.t:
The blessed martyr, Abū Miḥṣan al-Asadī, ally of Quraysh, one of the foremost first ones, a Badrī (البدري), of the people of Paradise.
The Prophet ﷺ appointed him over the expedition of al-Ghamr (1) , and they met no plot.
It was narrated from Umm Qays bint Miḥṣan, who said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died when ʿUkkāshah was forty-four years old.
She said: And he was killed a year after that at Buzākhah, in the caliphate (الخلافة) of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, in the year 12.
He was one of the most handsome of men (may Allah be pleased with him) (2) . ⟦1:307⟧
Such is this statement, but the correct view is that his killing was in the year 11. Ṭulayḥah al-Asadī killed him, who had apostatised and afterwards accepted Islam, and his Islam became good.
ʿUkkāshah had fought well on the day of Badr. His sword broke in his hand, and the Prophet ﷺ gave him a palm branch, or a stick, which by the permission of Allah became a sword in his hand. He fought with it and witnessed the campaigns with it (1) .
Narrating from him: أبو هريرة، وابن عباس، وغيرهما.
Khālid ibn al-Walīd had sent him out with Thābit ibn Aqram al-Anṣārī al-ʿAjlānī as scouts for him, on two horses. Ṭulayḥah overpowered them and killed them.
Thābit was a Badrī (البدري) of great standing, and he narrated nothing.
It is said: When the commander ibn Rawāḥah was struck on the day of Muʾtah, he handed the banner to Thābit ibn Aqram, but he could not bear it, so he handed it to Khālid and said: You know war better than I.

65.h: 61 - Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās ibn Zuhayr ibn Mālik al-Anṣārī *
65.t:
Ibn Imruʾ al-Qays ibn Mālik al-Aghar ibn Thaʿlabah ibn ⟦1:308⟧ Kaʿb ibn al-Khazraj ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj.
Abū Muḥammad, and it is said: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.
The orator of the Anṣār, one of the noble companions of Muḥammad ﷺ. He did not witness Badr; he witnessed Uḥud and the Pledge of Riḍwān.
His mother: Hind al-Ṭāʾiyyah.
It is said: rather Kabshah bint Wāqid ibn al-Iṭnābah.
His maternal brothers and sisters: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah and ʿAmrah bint Rawāḥah.
He was the husband of Jamīlah bint ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl, and she bore him Muḥammad.
Ibn Isḥāq said: It is said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a pact of brotherhood between him and ʿAmmār.
It is said: rather the brotherhood was between ʿAmmār and Ḥudhayfah.
He had a loud voice and was an eloquent orator.
الأنصاري: حدثني حميد، عن أنس، قال:
Thābit ibn Qays spoke on the arrival of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Medina and said:
We shall protect you from what we protect ourselves and our children from, so what is there for us?
He said: (Paradise).
They said: We are content (1) .
مالك، وغيره: عن ابن شهاب، عن إسماعيل بن محمد بن ثابت بن قيس:
That Thābit ibn Qays said: O Messenger of Allah! I fear that I have perished. Allah forbids us to love to be praised for what we have not done, and I find that I love praise; and Allah forbids us arrogance ⟦1:309⟧, and I am a man who loves beauty; and Allah forbids us to raise our voices above your voice, and I am a man of loud voice.
He said: (O Thābit! Are you not content to live praised, to be killed a martyr, and to enter Paradise (1)?).
Ayyūb narrated from ʿIkrimah, who said:
When there was revealed: “Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet”, the verse, [Qurʾān 49:2], Thābit ibn Qays said:
I used to raise my voice above his voice, so I am of the people of the Fire.
So he sat in his house, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ missed him and was told what had kept him sitting.
He said: (Rather, he is of the people of Paradise).
On the day of al-Yamāmah, when the people were routed, Thābit said:
Shame on these and on what they worship! Shame on these and on what they do! O company of the Anṣār! Clear the way for me, that I may perhaps suffer its heat for an hour.
A man was standing at a breach; he killed him, and was killed. ⟦1:310⟧
أيوب: عن ثمامة بن عبد الله، عن أنس، قال:
I came upon Thābit ibn Qays on the day of al-Yamāmah while he was perfuming himself for burial, and I said:
Uncle! Do you not see what the people have met?
He said: Now, my nephew.
ابن عون: حدثنا موسى بن أنس، عن أنس، قال:
I came to him while he was perfuming himself, and I said: Do you not see?
He said: Now, my nephew.
Then he came forward and said: Like this, away from our faces, we strike the enemy. What a bad habit you have given your opponents! This is not how we fought alongside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He fought until he was killed (1) .
حماد بن سلمة: أنبأنا ثابت، عن أنس:
That Thābit ibn Qays came on the day of al-Yamāmah having perfumed himself and put on two white garments, in which he was shrouded. The people had been routed, and he said:
O Allah, I declare myself innocent before You of what these have brought, and I apologise for what these have done. What a bad habit you have given your opponents! Leave us and them for an hour.
He charged and fought until he was killed. His coat of mail had been stolen, and a man saw him in a dream, who said to him: It is in a pot beneath a packsaddle, ⟦1:311⟧ in such and such a place.
He also gave him instructions. They looked and found the coat of mail as he had said, and carried out his instructions (1) .
سهيل: عن أبيه، عن أبي هريرة، قال:
The Prophet ﷺ said: (What an excellent man is Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās (2)).
And from al-Zuhrī: that a delegation of Tamīm came, and their orator boasted of many things.
The Prophet ﷺ said to Thābit ibn Qays: (Stand and answer their orator).
He stood, praised Allah and spoke eloquently, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims were pleased by his standing (3) .
He is the one whose wife Jamīlah came complaining of him, saying: O Messenger of Allah! Neither I nor Thābit ibn Qays.
He said: (Will you return his garden to him?).
She said: Yes. So she obtained a divorce from him for compensation (4) . ⟦1:312⟧
It is said: She bore Muḥammad afterwards, wrapped him in a cloth and sent him to Thābit, who brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He chewed a date and rubbed it in his mouth, named him Muḥammad, and arranged a wet nurse for him.
Al-Ḥākim said: Thābit was in command of the Anṣār on the day of al-Yamāmah. Then he narrated in his biography hadiths, among them:
From the narration of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir, who said:
حدثني عطاء الخراساني، قال:
I came to Medina and went to the daughter of Thābit ibn Qays, and she mentioned the story of her father. She said:
When “Do not raise your voices” was revealed, my father sat weeping, ... and he mentioned the hadith.
In it: When he was martyred, a man saw him and he said:
When I was killed, a man of the Muslims took my coat of mail and hid it. He covered it with a cooking pot and put a saddle on top of it. So go to the commander and inform him, and beware of saying: This is a dream, and so losing it. When you come to Medina, say to the caliph of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: I owe such and such a debt, and my slave so-and-so is freed. And beware of saying: This is a dream, and so losing it.
He came to him and informed him of the matter, and he carried out his testament. We know of no one after (1) death whose testament was carried out other than Thābit ibn Qays (may Allah be pleased with him (2)).
Muḥammad, Yaḥyā and ʿAbd Allāh, the sons of Thābit ibn Qays, were killed on the day of al-Ḥarrah.
By coincidence, the sons of Thābit ibn Qays ibn al-Khaṭīm al-Awsī al-Ẓafarī, namely ʿUmar, Muḥammad and Yazīd, were also killed on the day of al-Ḥarrah.
He too had companionship with the Prophet and a narration in the Sunan collections (السنن).
His father was among the foremost poets of the Aws, and died before Islam spread in Medina. And among ⟦1:313⟧ his descendants: ʿAdī ibn Thābit, hadith scholar (المحدث) of Kufa, but he is in fact ʿAdī ibn Abān ibn Thābit ibn Qays ibn al-Khaṭīm ibn ʿAmr ibn Yazīd ibn Sawād ibn Ẓafar al-Ẓafarī, attributed to his grandfather.

66.h: 62 - Ṭulayḥah ibn Khuwaylid ibn Nawfal al-Asadī * ⟦1:316⟧
66.t:
The valiant hero who charged again and again, a Companion (الصحابي) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, one whose courage is used as a proverb.
He accepted Islam in the year 9, then apostatised and wronged himself, and claimed prophethood in Najd. He had wars with the Muslims, then was defeated and forsaken, and joined the Ghassānid house of Jafnah in Syria. Then he repented and accepted Islam, and his Islam became good, when al-Ṣiddīq died, and he assumed the state of pilgrim sanctity for the Hajj.
When ʿUmar saw him, he said:
O Ṭulayḥah! I do not love you after your killing of ʿUkkāshah ibn Miḥṣan and Thābit ibn Aqram.
They had been scouts for Khālid (1) on the day of Buzākhah, and Ṭulayḥah and his brother killed them. Then he witnessed al-Qādisiyyah and Nahāwand.
ʿUmar wrote to Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ: Consult Ṭulayḥah on the affairs of war, but do not give him any office.
Muḥammad ibn Saʿd said: Ṭulayḥah was counted as equal to a thousand horsemen for his courage and his might.
I say: He fought well on the day of Nahāwand (2) , then was martyred (may Allah be pleased with him and pardon him). ⟦1:317⟧

67.h: 63 - Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ ibn ʿAmr ibn Abī Zuhayr al-Anṣārī *
67.t:
Ibn Mālik ibn Imruʾ al-Qays ibn Mālik ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Kaʿb ibn al-Khazraj ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj.
Al-Anṣārī, al-Khazrajī, al-Ḥārithī (1) , the Badrī (البدري), the chief, the martyr, between whom and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (2) ibn ʿAwf the Prophet ﷺ made a pact of brotherhood. He resolved to give ʿAbd al-Raḥmān half of his wealth and to divorce one of his two wives so that he might marry her, but ʿAbd al-Raḥmān declined that and prayed for him. He was one of the chiefs on the night of ʿAqabah.
ابن إسحاق: عن محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن أبي صعصعة:
That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Who is the man who will look into what has become of Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ for me?).
A man of the Anṣār said: I will.
So he went out going about among the slain until he found Saʿd wounded, fixed (3) at his last breath.
He said: O Saʿd! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered me to see whether you are among the living or among the dead?
He said: I am among the dead, so convey my greeting of peace to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and say:
Saʿd says: May Allah reward you on my behalf with the best that He has rewarded a prophet on behalf of his community. And convey my greeting of peace to your people, ⟦1:318⟧ and say to them:
Saʿd says to you: You will have no excuse before Allah if harm reaches your Prophet while an eye of you still blinks (1) .
عبد الله بن محمد بن عقيل: عن جابر بن عبد الله، قال:
The wife of Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ came with her two daughters by Saʿd, and said:
O Messenger of Allah! These are the two daughters of Saʿd. Their father was killed with you at Uḥud as a martyr, and their uncle has taken their wealth and left them no wealth, and they cannot be married unless they have wealth.
He said: (Allah will decide in that).
Then the verse of the inheritance shares was revealed, and he sent for their uncle and said: (Give the two daughters of Saʿd two thirds, and give their mother an eighth, and what remains is yours (2)).
عن خارجة بن زيد بن ثابت، عن أبيه، قال:
The Prophet ﷺ sent me on the day of Uḥud to look for Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ, and he said to me: (If you see him, convey to him my greeting of peace, and say to him:
The Messenger of Allah says to you: How do you find yourself?).
I went round among the slain and found him at his last breath, with seventy wounds upon him, and I told him.
He said: Peace be upon the Messenger of Allah, and upon you. Say to him:
O Messenger of Allah! I find the scent of Paradise. And say to my people, the Anṣār:
You will have no excuse before Allah if harm reaches the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while among you an eyelid (3) still blinks.
He said: And his soul departed - ⟦1:319⟧ may Allah be pleased with him.
Al-Bayhaqī transmitted it, then related it with similar wording by the route of Ibn Isḥāq, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Ṣaʿṣaʿah, similar to what has preceded (1) .
Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr reported from Mālik ibn Anas:
That the Prophet ﷺ said: (Who will bring us news of Saʿd?).
A man said: I will.
He went about among the slain and found him with a breath of life left, and said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to bring him news of you.
He said: Go, and convey to him my greeting of peace, and inform him that I have been stabbed with twelve stabs, and that they have pierced my vital parts (2) .

68.h: 64 - Maʿn ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Jadd ibn al-ʿAjlān al-Anṣārī *
68.t:
Al-ʿAjlānī, al-ʿAqabī, the Badrī (البدري), of the allies of Banū Mālik ibn ʿAwf, one of the leaders of the Anṣār. He used to write Arabic before Islam.
Ibn Saʿd said: He has descendants today.
He narrated: الزهري، عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله، عن ابن عباس:
That Maʿn ibn ʿAdī was one of the two men who met Abū Bakr and ʿUmar as they were heading for the portico of Banū Sāʿidah, ⟦1:320⟧ and said to Abū Bakr and ʿUmar:
You need not go near them; settle your matter.
ʿUrwah said: It reached us that the people wept for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
If only we had died before him, we fear that we shall be tried after him.
Maʿn said: But I, by Allah, do not like that I died before him, until I believe in him dead as I believed in him alive (1) .
Ibn al-Athīr said: Maʿn ibn ʿAdī ibn al-ʿAjlān al-Balawī, ally of Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, one of the men of ʿAqabah, a Badrī (البدري), well known.
I say: He is the brother of ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Jadd ibn al-ʿAjlān al-Balawī, ally of Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf. ʿĀṣim was the master of Banū al-ʿAjlān, and he is the father of Abū al-Badāḥ ibn ʿĀṣim.
ʿĀṣim also witnessed Badr, and his hadith is in the four Sunan collections (السنن).
Maʿn was among those martyred on the day of al-Yamāmah, in the year 12.

69.h: 65 - ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Mālik al-Anṣārī *
69.t:
Ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿUbayd ibn Mālik ibn Sālim - and Sālim is the one called al-Ḥublā, because of the size of his belly - ibn Ghanm ibn ʿAwf ibn al-Khazraj al-Anṣārī, al-Khazrajī, whose father is known as Ibn Salūl, the notorious hypocrite.
Salūl al-Khuzāʿiyyah is the mother of Ubayy ⟦1:321⟧ mentioned.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh was one of the leaders of the Companions (الصحابي) and their best. His name was al-Ḥubāb, and his father was called by it as a patronymic, but the Prophet ﷺ changed it and named him ʿAbd Allāh.
He witnessed Badr and what came after.
Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mandah mentioned that his nose was struck on the day of Uḥud, and the Prophet ﷺ ordered him to make a nose of gold (1) .
More likely in this matter is what was narrated from ʿĀʾishah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, that he said:
My front tooth fell out, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered me to make a tooth of gold (2) .
ʿAbd Allāh was martyred on the day of al-Yamāmah. His father had died in the year 9, and the Prophet ﷺ clothed him in his shirt, prayed over him and asked forgiveness for him out of honour to his son, until there was revealed: “And never pray over any of them who has died, and do not stand at his grave (3)”, the verse, [Qurʾān 9:89]. ⟦1:322⟧
He had been an obeyed chief; before the Prophet ﷺ migrated, the people of Medina had resolved to make him their king, but his affair collapsed, and he gained neither this world nor the Hereafter - we ask Allah for well-being.

70.h: 66 - ʿIkrimah ibn Abī Jahl ʿAmr ibn Hishām al-Makhzūmī * (ت)
70.t:
Ibn al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Makhzūm ibn Yaqaẓah ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy.
The noble, the chief, the martyr, Abū ʿUthmān al-Qurashī al-Makhzūmī al-Makkī.
When his father was killed, the leadership of Banū Makhzūm passed to ʿIkrimah. Then he accepted Islam, and his Islam became thoroughly good (1) .
Ibn Abī Mulaykah said: When ʿIkrimah strove hard in an oath, he would say: No, by Him who saved me on the day of Badr.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered Mecca, ʿIkrimah fled from it, and Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf, ⟦1:323⟧ so the Prophet ﷺ sent to give them both safe-conduct and pardoned them, and they came to him.
Abū al-Qāsim Ibn ʿAsākir gave his reports exhaustively (1) .
Al-Tirmidhī transmitted it by the route of Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, from ʿIkrimah - and he did not meet him:
That the Prophet ﷺ said to him: (Welcome to the rider who has migrated).
He said: I said: O Messenger of Allah! By Allah, I will not leave any expense that I spent against you without spending the like of it in the cause of Allah (2) .
ʿIkrimah left no offspring.
Al-Shāfiʿī said: He was praiseworthy in his trials in Islam (may Allah be pleased with him).
Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī said: ʿIkrimah dismounted on the day of al-Yarmūk and fought fiercely, then was martyred, and they found upon him over seventy stabs, arrow wounds and sword blows.
ʿUrwah, Ibn Saʿd and a group said: He was killed on the day of Ajnādayn.

71.h: 67 - ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥarām ibn Thaʿlabah al-Anṣārī *
71.t:
Ibn Ḥarām ibn Kaʿb ibn Ghanm ibn Kaʿb ibn Salimah ibn Saʿd ibn ʿAlī ibn ⟦1:324⟧ Asad ibn Sārdah ibn Tazīd (1) ibn Jusham ibn al-Khazraj al-Anṣārī, al-Salamī, Abū Jābir.
One of the chiefs on the night of ʿAqabah; he witnessed Badr and was martyred on the day of Uḥud.
شعبة: عن ابن المنكدر، عن جابر:
When my father was killed on the day of Uḥud, I began to uncover his face and weep, and the Companions (الصحابي) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to forbid me, though he did not forbid me, and my paternal aunt began to weep over him.
The Prophet ﷺ said: (Whether you weep over him or do not weep over him (2) , the angels did not cease to shade him with their wings until you lifted him (3)).
شريك: عن الأسود بن قيس، عن نبيح العنزي، عن جابر، قال:
My father and my maternal uncle were struck on the day of Uḥud, and my mother brought them, having laid them across a camel, and came with them to Medina.
Then a caller called out: Bury the slain where they fell. So they were returned and buried where they fell (4) . ⟦1:325⟧
Mālik said: He and ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ were shrouded in one shroud.
Al-Awzāʿī said: عن الزهري، عن جابر:
That when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to bury the martyrs of Uḥud, he said: (Wrap them with their wounds, for I am a witness over them).
And my father was shrouded in a striped cloak (1) .
Ibn Saʿd said:
They said: ʿAbd Allāh was the first to be killed on the day of Uḥud. He was ruddy and bald, not tall, and ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ was tall. They were buried together by the watercourse, and the flood dug them out, with a striped cloak upon them. ʿAbd Allāh had received a wound in his face, and his hand was upon his wound; when his hand was removed, the blood gushed forth, so it was put back and the blood stopped.
Jābir said: I saw my father in his grave as if asleep, and nothing of his condition had changed, and between that and his death were forty-six years. They were moved to another place, and they brought them out fresh, their limbs supple (2) .
أبو الزبير: عن جابر، قال:
We were called out to our slain when Muʿāwiyah made the spring flow, and we brought them out with their bodies soft and their limbs flexible (3) .
ابن أبي نجيح: عن عطاء، عن جابر، قال:
A man was buried with my father, and my heart was not at ease until I brought him out and buried him alone (4) . ⟦1:326⟧
سعيد بن يزيد أبو مسلمة: عن أبي نضرة، عن جابر، قال: my father said:
I hope to be among the first to be struck tomorrow, so I charge you to treat my daughters well.
He was struck, and I buried him with another, but my heart would not let me be until I exhumed him and buried him alone after six months, and the earth had consumed nothing of him except part of the fat of his ear (1) .
Al-Shaʿbī: Jābir narrated to me that his father died leaving a debt.
He said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
My father left a debt upon him, and we have nothing but what comes from his palms, so come with me lest the creditors treat me harshly.
He said: He walked around one of the date threshing floors and prayed, then sat upon it, and paid them what was owed them, and as much remained as he had given them (2) .
And there are hadiths on this in the Ṣaḥīḥ.
Ibn al-Madīnī said: حدثنا موسى بن إبراهيم، حدثنا طلحة بن خراش، سمع جابرا يقول:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: (Shall I not tell you that Allah spoke to your father face to face, and said:
O My servant! Ask Me and I shall give you.
He said: I ask You to return me to the world, that I may be killed for You a second time.
He said: It has already preceded from Me that they shall not return to it.
He said: My Lord! Then convey to those I left behind.
So Allah revealed: “Do not think of those who were killed in the cause of Allah as dead; rather they are alive with their Lord, provided for” [Qurʾān, Āl ʿImrān (1) 3:169]). ⟦1:327⟧
A similar report was narrated from the hadith of ʿĀʾishah.
ابن إسحاق: حدثنا عاصم بن عمر، عن عبد الرحمن بن جابر، عن أبيه:
He heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, when the Companions (الصحابي) of Uḥud were mentioned: (By Allah, I wish that I had been left behind with the companions at the foot of the mountain).
He means: that I had been killed with them ﷺ (2) .
